cohort: The study included 120 pregnant women in their second or third trimester attending antenatal care at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Multiple regression analysis revealed that anterior placental location was associated with an increased risk of gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, and cesarean delivery, as well as lower birth weight.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were highest in the lateral placental location group, and anterior placental location was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery.
cross-section timing: Second or third trimester of pregnancy
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome, no specific range for inclusion.
gest_age: Participants were in their second or third trimester.
